result.title: Learning World Models through Contrastive Identification of Actions
result.summary: Latent world models enable goal-directed planning from offline visual data, but prediction alone does not specify which action-related distinctions their representations should preserve. Inverse dynamics provides auxiliary supervision, yet squared-error action regression rewards additional information only through changes in the conditional action mean. We propose Contrastive Identification of Actions (CIA), which identifies the executed action among alternatives sampled from a history-conditioned behavior proposal. Comparing actions plausible in the same context targets information supplied by the next latent beyond history. Under exact behavior matching, we show that CIA can reward action information that leaves optimal inverse-regression error unchanged, and verify this distinction through a controlled learning example. CIA achieves higher planner-averaged mean success than the base world model and a regression inverse-dynamics baseline across five visual control benchmarks, without modifying the planner.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Contrastive Identification of Actions（CIA），在带有行为提议的世界模型中让模型从同一历史下采样的候选动作中辨识实际执行动作，以对比式逆动力学替代平方误差回归，从而激励下一时刻 latent 携带历史之外的动作信息，并在五个视觉控制基准上验证规划成功率提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心是「用对比目标筛选 latent 中应保留哪些信息」，与 LVR 中状态内容选择、训练监督和贡献分配问题可能相关，可供核查该辨识式监督是否也适用于推理期 latent 轨迹的有效性判别。
